title: Strategic Account Signal Normalizer and Roadmap Safeguard
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Create a defensible, auditable system that normalizes disparate top-account signals into a single prioritization score and attaches a roadmap safeguard (runbook + SLA hooks) that ensures predictable commitments for escalations. This ticket delivers the scoring spec, acceptance criteria, communication templates, and rollout plan for PM+Sales+SRE workflows.

Background: Sales and CS surface high-urgency asks from strategic accounts (legal/regulatory, performance regressions, feature gating). Current intake is ad-hoc: manual emails, Slack pings, and one-off GitHub issues. That leads to unclear commitments, missed SLAs, and executive escalation. We need a repeatable mechanism that: (a) aggregates signals (usage, ARR, severity, security/regulatory, exec advocacy), (b) normalizes and de-biases them, (c) produces a ranked queue for roadmap consideration, and (d) provides explicit safeguard runbooks for escalations that map to release/rollback/communication paths.

Signal inputs (initial scope):
- Revenue & ARR motion (ARR tier, renewal delta)
- Product usage (token volume, route-specific latency/error spikes)
- Incident severity & SLO breach history (from SRE)
- Compliance/regulatory flags (legal/enterprise requests)
- Exec advocacy / account escalations (Sales/Customer Success verified)
- Strategic partner status (co-marketing, integrations)

Normalizer design summary (proposal):
1) Feature mapping layer: fuzzy-match incoming ask to canonical feature buckets (e.g., routing/policy, KV caching, batching, RBAC, audit logs). Maintains a small taxonomy to avoid duplicate asks.
2) Signal weighting: base weights for ARR (0.25), incident severity (0.30), usage delta (0.15), compliance (0.20), exec advocacy (0.10). Weights configurable per cohort (enterprise vs mid-market).
3) Noise suppression: apply exponential decay to signals older than 60 days; apply outlier clamp for single-session spikes to avoid noisy elevation.
4) Manual override layer: Product Lead can apply an override token with reason logged; overrides must include acceptance criteria and timebox.
5) Explainability metadata: every score must output top-3 contributing signals and a short rationale string for audit.

Acceptance criteria (must be met to close ticket):
- Spec doc with taxonomy and mapping rules published to Confluence (link below).
- Normalizer accepts synthetic test vectors and produces expected relative rankings for 12 curated scenarios (unit test harness).
- Escalation safeguard runbook drafted with SLA tiers, communication templates (Customer, VP, Engineering), and rollback criteria.
- Console dashboard wireframe showing ranked queue and per-account score decomposition (token-level cost/latency link).
- Integration checklist for SRE and Sales (SRE log ingest, Sales verification workflow) with owners assigned.

Trade-offs / decisions to call out:
- Deterministic vs ML: start deterministic weighted model for explainability and auditability; keep hooks for future ML re-ranking.
- Weight sensitivity: small changes shift order; we'll add a stability penalty so recently-triaged items don't flip-flop (cooldown window = 14 days).
- Gaming risk: Sales could over-index exec advocacy. Mitigation: require Sales verification and timestamped evidence; track override metrics.

Runbook highlights (escalation flow):
- Triage within 4 business hours by Customer Success lead.
- If incident severity >= Sev2 or compliance flag = true -> auto-create incident bridge and tag ENG on-call.
- Timeboxed commitment window: for P0 strategic asks, PM posts proposed scope within 5 business days; engineering sends feasibility and deliverability estimate within 10 business days.
- Canary + fallback policy: new work to be feature-flagged with canary rollout to affected accounts, default fallback to nearest compatible model variant and rate-limited burst capacity on Dedicated for the customer.
- Communication templates (customer-facing & internal) appended to Confluence doc.

Metrics / success criteria post-rollout:
- Median time from escalation intake to PM proposed scope <= 5 business days.
- Percent of escalations with documented acceptance criteria >= 95%.
- SLA adherence for committed P0 items >= 90% over first 6 months.
- Reduction in exec escalation repeats by 40% quarter-over-quarter.
